title: Addiction-treatment administration by order in a registered opioid treatment program
rule_summary: 105 CMR 700.004(B)(9)(e) authorises a pharmacist to administer controlled substances in an Opioid Treatment Program PURSUANT TO AN ORDER and in accordance with Department guidance. Circular DCP 26-03-124 states that a pharmacist may administer medications for addiction treatment, INCLUDING METHADONE, pursuant to an order, ONLY in a registered opioid treatment program. The instrument is an order rather than a prescription, and the setting is closed.
exam_relevance: Tests a route whose setting and whose instrument both differ from the ordinary administration pathway.

authority.name: Massachusetts Department of Public Health regulations
Circular Letter DCP 26-03-124, Pharmacist Administration of Medications, 11 March 2026
authority.section: Note following the conditions for Dispensing by Administration

common_confusions: Assuming a valid prescription opens this route in a community pharmacy
Assuming buprenorphine and methadone travel the same pathway in every setting
Overlooking that the programme must be a registered opioid treatment program
verification_notes: Read verbatim in the current official publication on 2026-08-20 during Batch 3 tranche B3-D authoring under Issue #91. A fresh independent legal and full-bank realism audit is still required before release.
